A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GP-UCB regret-analysis work. Their complete main text, Figure 1, equations, and Appendices A–C are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figure 1 reports an original one-dimensional Bayesian-optimization simulation, including a sampled Matérn-GP function, query histograms, and information-gain trajectories for GP-UCB and MVR over 200 steps.

after.justification: v2 retains Figure 1's original simulation results: the sampled function, 200-step query histograms, and information-gain trajectories for GP-UCB and MVR.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the GP posterior updates, and the confidence-width schedule in Equation (6) are unchanged. The revision strengthens the analysis of the same GP-UCB procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same one-dimensional synthetic Bayesian-optimization scenario in Figure 1. No datasets, evaluation domains, or additional test scenarios are introduced in the appendices.

E2.justification: Figure 1 retains MVR as the comparator to GP-UCB and the idealized Case I reference curve. No evaluated comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Figure 1 retains the Matérn smoothness parameter ν = 5/2, noise variance σ² = 3, 200 query steps, and the same query-frequency and information-gain measurements.

E4.justification: The illustrative analysis of query concentration and information-gain growth in Figure 1 is unchanged. Neither version adds further ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness experiments, or empirical case studies.

E5.justification: Simulation reporting is unchanged: neither version supplies seeds, repeated-run counts, error bars, confidence intervals, or significance tests for Figure 1.

E6.justification: Figure 1's sampled function, histograms, and information-gain curves are identical. Its findings of slower information-gain growth than MVR and behavior resembling Case I from t ≥ 30 are retained; no empirical result entries change.

T1.justification: Lemmas 4–6 and Appendix A are substantively revised. Retaining geometric weights in Appendix A.1 improves the SE regret bound from O(sqrt(T) ln^2 T) to O(sqrt(T) ln T). Appendix A.3 derives polylogarithmic Matérn lenient regret, allowing Theorem 3 to drop 4ν² + 2νd ≥ d² while retaining 2ν + d ≤ ν². Further corrections address the constant after Equation (8), quadratic-growth constants in Appendix A.2, and the SE log-log exponent in Appendix A.3.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction strengthen the central SE guarantee from O(sqrt(T) ln^2 T) to O(sqrt(T) ln T), now claiming improvement over the previous GP-UCB bound for every d ≥ 1 rather than d > 3. The main Matérn guarantee also covers a broader smoothness–dimension range.

C2.justification: New footnotes to Theorem 3 explain that the previous extra Matérn restriction resulted from omitted lenient-regret proof steps and that the extra SE logarithmic factor was avoidable. Section 4's remaining limitations and Figure 1's interpretation are unchanged.

D1.justification: The algorithm specification and disclosed simulation settings are unchanged. No implementation instructions, hardware or runtime information, or code/data access information is added or removed.

R1.justification: The introduction broadens the claimed SE advantage over Srinivas et al. [48] from d > 3 to all d ≥ 1. The related-work section and all 59 references are unchanged, so the positioning revision is localized.

P1.justification: v2 adds two correction footnotes, rewrites Appendix A.3 into separate kernel cases, and makes limited wording and notation corrections. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: The new footnotes and shortened Lemma 6 alter local page layout, while the expanded Appendix A.3 reflows subsequent material. Figure 1's panels, axes, legends, and caption, and Algorithm 1's display remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The revised derivations resolve important weaknesses in this primarily theoretical paper: they tighten SE regret from O(sqrt(T) ln^2 T) to O(sqrt(T) ln T) and remove an unnecessary Matérn restriction. Appendices A.1–A.3 supply the supporting steps and correct additional algebraic and logarithmic terms. These changes substantially strengthen the central guarantee and its mathematical support, while preserving the empirical illustration and the qualifications concerning expected regret and optimality.
